visual.general_description: Graphical abstract summarizing cohort-level results of the series.
visual.detailed_description: A landscape infographic with a purple title banner reading Morganella morganii Urinary Tract Infection in Jordanian Children: Tertiary Hospital Experience and the logo Infection and Chemotherapy. The left column has Background (kidney and baby icons, a map and flag of Jordan, three bullets about UTI risk, kidney damage and Jordanian children with M. morganii UTI) and Methods (hospital and laboratory icons; bullets: retrospective review 2017-2022 and demographics, clinical presentation, labs, imaging and susceptibility data collected). The Result panel shows a horizontal stacked bar for Male 22.2% and Female 78.8%, a bar chart of the most common symptoms (Fever 55.6%, Malodorous urine 44.4%, Vomiting 22.2%), a box listing Morganella morganii Sensitive: amikacin, cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam and Resistant: amoxicillin-clavulanate, nitrofurantoin, a pie chart with 56% and 44% beside text saying neurogenic bladder and myelomeningocele were each present in 44% of cases, and 3.35 median age in years. A purple Conclusion banner reads that M. morganii should be considered in pediatric UTIs, especially among children with urinary tract anomalies or catheter use, and that its distinct resistance profile is critical for empiric therapy. No patient photographs, radiographs or individual-level data appear.
